text: Noss Manâ€™s religions reflect his human need to feel at home in the universe and comfortable among his neighbors.

chapter_title: part miiâ€™sic, vocal music for two or more
text: He has always sensed that he cannot stand alone; that good work- able relations with his neighbors matter to him; that since mysterious powers in Nature and Society will not let him alone but affect him at every step, he must be in harmony either with them, with the great lords and kings among them, or with the one originative being that has brought the whole world into being and in some sovereign way commands all its processes.

chapter_title: part miiâ€™sic, vocal music for two or more
text: The religions of the past (not treated in this article) have all reflected these human needs and concerns.
text_raw:
The religions of the past (not treated in this article) have all 
reflected these human needs and concerns.

chapter_title: part miiâ€™sic, vocal music for two or more
text: The Neanderthal Man and his talented successors, the Cro-Magnon men of France, Spain, and Africa, very evidently sought good rela- tions with nonhuman powers that pervaded the natural world and affected human destiny.
text_raw:
The Neanderthal 
Man and his talented successors, the Cro-Magnon men of 
France, Spain, and Africa, very evidently sought good rela- 
tions with nonhuman powers that pervaded the natural 
world and affected human destiny.

chapter_title: part miiâ€™sic, vocal music for two or more
text: The great national relig- ions of the past in Egypt, Mesopotamia, Greece, Rome, and Northern Europe were constantly concerned with great lords and kings among the spirits and powers operating on earth and in the heavens, and they showed an equal concern as to the destiny of man in this life and the next.
text_raw:
The great national relig- 
ions of the past in Egypt, Mesopotamia, Greece, Rome, and 
Northern Europe were constantly concerned with great 
lords and kings among the spirits and powers operating on 
earth and in the heavens, and they showed an equal concern 
as to the destiny of man in this life and the next.

chapter_title: part miiâ€™sic, vocal music for two or more
text: We shall see that the living religions of man today are similarly motivated.
text_raw:
We shall see that the living religions of man today are 
similarly motivated.

chapter_title: part miiâ€™sic, vocal music for two or more
text: PRIMITIVE RELIGIONS Religions of peoples who live close to nature, in relatively isolated societies not yet penetrated by the technology and culture of highly organized industrial societies, are said to be primitive.
text_raw:
PRIMITIVE RELIGIONS 
Religions of peoples who live close to nature, in relatively 
isolated societies not yet penetrated by the technology and 
culture of highly organized industrial societies, are said to be 
primitive.

chapter_title: part miiâ€™sic, vocal music for two or more
text: They include the Australian aborigines, the pygmies of Africa, the jungle tribes of India and Southeast Asia, the natives of New Guinea and of portions of the South Seas, the Indians of the Upper Amazon and of Central America, and certain Eskimo tribes.
text_raw:
They include the Australian aborigines, the 
pygmies of Africa, the jungle tribes of India and Southeast 
Asia, the natives of New Guinea and of portions of the 
South Seas, the Indians of the Upper Amazon and of Central 
America, and certain Eskimo tribes.

chapter_title: part miiâ€™sic, vocal music for two or more
text: Many primitive groups of a generation ago are now under- going transformation through cultural, educational, and technological changes that are breaking up the established patterns of the past; but primitives are in general resistant to such changes.
text_raw:
Many primitive groups of a generation ago are now under- 
going transformation through cultural, educational, and 
technological changes that are breaking up the established 
patterns of the past; but primitives are in general resistant 
to such changes.

chapter_title: part miiâ€™sic, vocal music for two or more
text: The traditional customs and beliefs are their means of adaptation to environment; furthermore, they unify the tribe, are comfortable for the individual in that they provide each group member with a role to play that is approved in advance, and are above all sacred, because hallowed by ancestors and divine powers, and therefore binding.
text_raw:
The traditional customs and beliefs are 
their means of adaptation to environment; furthermore, they 
unify the tribe, are comfortable for the individual in that 
they provide each group member with a role to play that is 
approved in advance, and are above all sacred, because 
hallowed by ancestors and divine powers, and therefore 
binding.

chapter_title: part miiâ€™sic, vocal music for two or more
text: Besides this, they satisfy basic biological and psychological needs.
text_raw:
Besides this, they satisfy basic biological and 
psychological needs.

chapter_title: part miiâ€™sic, vocal music for two or more
text: Many primitive customs and beliefs strike persons trained in scientific method as naive and supersititous, but they in fact reflect the kind of realism and common sense which follow from taking sensations at face valueâ€”a characteristic of primitives in general.
text_raw:
Many primitive customs and beliefs 
strike persons trained in scientific method as naive and 
supersititous, but they in fact reflect the kind of realism and 
common sense which follow from taking sensations at face 
valueâ€”a characteristic of primitives in general.

chapter_title: part miiâ€™sic, vocal music for two or more
text: Moreover the individual seldom questions what the group feels or senses to be the case.
text_raw:
Moreover 
the individual seldom questions what the group feels or 
senses to be the case.

chapter_title: part miiâ€™sic, vocal music for two or more
text: Hence, while primitives have beliefs and practices that the experimental methods of science would seem to discredit, they find them quite true and necessary.
text_raw:
Hence, while primitives have beliefs 
and practices that the experimental methods of science would 
seem to discredit, they find them quite true and necessary.

chapter_title: part miiâ€™sic, vocal music for two or more
text: Some common features of primitive belief and practice may be discerned, as follows:
text_raw:
Some common features of primitive belief and practice may 
be discerned, as follows:

chapter_title: part miiâ€™sic, vocal music for two or more
text: Reverence for the Sacred Events, persons, and places in any degree uncanny, mysterious, or creditable with super- natural power are sacred or holy.
text_raw:
Reverence for the Sacred Events, persons, and places 
in any degree uncanny, mysterious, or creditable with super- 
natural power are sacred or holy.

chapter_title: part miiâ€™sic, vocal music for two or more
text: Included in this very large category are most rites and ceremonies and those who con- duct or commandingly participate in them.
text_raw:
Included in this very large 
category are most rites and ceremonies and those who con- 
duct or commandingly participate in them.

chapter_title: part miiâ€™sic, vocal music for two or more
text: The traditions of the tribe are hallowed by the ancestors who passed them on.
text_raw:
The traditions 
of the tribe are hallowed by the ancestors who passed them 
on.

chapter_title: part miiâ€™sic, vocal music for two or more
text: Many places and objects are sacred, such as groves of trees or fetishes (objects thought to embody spirits or magic powers).
text_raw:
Many places and objects are sacred, such as groves of 
trees or fetishes (objects thought to embody spirits or magic 
powers).

chapter_title: part miiâ€™sic, vocal music for two or more
text: The most common reason for considering a person, place, or action taboo or to be abstained from is that it is sacred and has the power to cause quick good or ill.
text_raw:
The most common reason for considering a person, 
place, or action taboo or to be abstained from is that it is 
sacred and has the power to cause quick good or ill.

chapter_title: part miiâ€™sic, vocal music for two or more
text: The presence of the sacred, because it arouses anxiety, is also the chief cause of religious and magical rituals seeking reassur- ance and favorable outcomes.
text_raw:
The 
presence of the sacred, because it arouses anxiety, is also the 
chief cause of religious and magical rituals seeking reassur- 
ance and favorable outcomes.

chapter_title: part miiâ€™sic, vocal music for two or more
text: Intermingling of Magic and Religion Religious rituals are persuasive in intent, while magical rituals seek to be coercive.
text_raw:

are persuasive in intent, while magical rituals seek to be 
coercive.

chapter_title: part miiâ€™sic, vocal music for two or more
text: But in most primitive ceremonies it is hard to disentangle the magical and religious elements; the words may be persuasive in form, but taken together they may carry the guarantee of a compulsive effect on gods and spirits, while, on the other hand, magical rites may mingle prayers with commands.

text: This should be borne in mind when con- sidering the topics that follow.

text: Veneration and Worship of Many Powers and Spirits Primitives reverence and at times worship multitudes of powers and spirits, some of which have the status of gods.

Primitives reverence and at times worship multitudes of 
powers and spirits, some of which have the status of gods.

text: Venerated or worshiped are stones, plants, trees, many kinds of animals and reptiles, fire, voleanoes, rivers and lakes, sun, moon, stars, mountains, and many other animate and inanimate things.

of animals and reptiles, fire, voleanoes, rivers and lakes,

selves alive with power in every part; or they may be con-

magic wards off happenings and productive magic brings them

Amendment 12 
(Ratified July 27, 1804) 
The Electors shall meet in their respective states and vote by ballot for President and Vice-President, one of whom, at least, shall not be an inhabitant of the same state with them- selves; they shall name in their ballots the person voted for as President, and in distinet ballots the person voted for as Vice-President, and they shall make distinct lists of all per- sons voted for as President, and of all persons voted for as Vice-President, and of the number of votes for each, which lists they shall sign and certify, and transmit sealed to the seat of the government of the United States, directed to the President of the Senate;â€”The President of the Senate shall, in the presence of the Senate and House of Representa- tives, open all the certificates and the votes shall then be counted;â€”The person having the greatest number of votes for President, shall be the President, if such number be a majority of the whole number of Electors appointed; and if no person have such majority, then from the persons having the highest numbers not exceeding three on the list of those voted for as President, the House of Representatives shall choose immediately, by ballot, the President.
